t: Minimum Cost to Merge Sorted Lists
o: Repeatedly merge two lists paying len(a)+len(b)+|median(a)-median(b)| until one remains; ≤ 12 lists, total length ≤ 2000. The merged result of any subset is always the sorted union of its members, independent of merge order — only the cost accumulates differently. This screams bitmask DP over subsets: dp[S] = minimum cost to fuse exactly the lists in S into one list. The median of any subset's union can be queried with a binary search over values counting elements across the member lists.
k: The content of a merged list depends only on the set of original lists, enabling subset DP.
Median of a subset = k-th smallest of the union, found by binary-searching the value and counting via bisect in each member list.
With m ≤ 12 there are ≤ 4096 subsets; transitions are m per subset.

a.n: Bitmask DP with Precomputed Subset Medians
a.i: Precompute for every mask its total length and its median (the (len+1)//2-th smallest of the union, which handles both parities as the left middle). Then dp over masks: dp[{i}] = 0, and dp[S | 1<<i] = min(dp[S] + len(S) + len(i) + |med(S) - med(i)|). The answer is dp[full].
s: Precompute tot[mask] = sum of lengths, via tot[mask] = tot[mask without lowest bit] + len(lowest).
Compute med[mask] for all masks with a k-th-smallest binary search over the globally sorted values, counting elements ≤ x across member lists using bisect.
Initialize dp[1<<i] = 0; iterate masks ascending, relaxing dp[mask | 1<<i] for i not in mask with cost tot[mask] + len(i) + abs(med[mask] - med[i]).
a.t: O(2^m · (m + L log V · m)) roughly — 4096 masks, each median via binary search over values with an O(total log len) counting step; comfortably fast for m ≤ 12, total length ≤ 2000
a.sp: O(2^m + L) — DP/median tables over masks plus the sorted value array

w: The key insight to voice early: merge results depend only on sets, so Huffman-style greedy pairing does not apply directly (median costs are order-dependent) and subset DP is natural. Pitfall: median definition — left middle for even lengths, i.e., k = (len+1)//2; verify with a 4-element list. Also mind 64-bit costs. Follow-ups: what if merges had to respect a fixed pairing tree, or if the cost were |mean(a) - mean(b)| (then prefix sums give subset means in O(1)).
